title: The Python Tutorial: Data Structures
section: 5.1 More on Lists; 5.3 Tuples and Sequences
text: Lists are mutable data structures. Methods such as append, insert, remove, pop, sort, and reverse change the existing list. Tuples are immutable, although a tuple can contain a separate mutable object such as a list.

title: The Python Tutorial: Data Structures
text: Tuples are immutable: assigning to an individual tuple item is not allowed. A tuple may contain a mutable object, but that does not make the tuple's own item bindings mutable.

title: The Python Tutorial: Data Structures
text: Iterating over a dictionary, including list(dict), produces keys in insertion order. Calling sorted on the dictionary keys is a separate way to obtain sorted order.

title: The Python Tutorial: Data Structures
text: A set is an unordered collection with no duplicate elements. Iterating over a set or printing it can produce elements in an order different from what a reader expects.

title: The Python Tutorial: Data Structures
text: A list comprehension evaluates an expression for items selected by its for and optional if clauses, producing a new list.

title: The Python Tutorial: Data Structures
text: Dictionary subscription with a missing key raises KeyError. The get method returns None by default for a missing key, or returns the caller-provided default value.

title: The Python Tutorial: Data Structures
text: A list can represent a queue, but inserts and pops at the beginning are slow because the other elements must shift. The tutorial recommends collections.deque for efficient operations at both ends.

title: Built-in Functions
text: The built-in sorted function is guaranteed to be stable. A stable sort preserves the relative order of elements that compare equal.

title: The Python Language Reference: Compound Statements
text: Executing a function definition binds a function object to its name. The function body is not executed by defining it; the body runs when the function is called.

title: The Python Language Reference: Compound Statements
text: A for loop's optional else suite runs when the loop finishes normally because the iterator is exhausted. It does not run when a break statement terminates the loop.

title: The Python Tutorial: Errors and Exceptions
text: If an exception is not handled by an except clause, it is propagated to the caller and may continue up the call stack.

title: The Python Tutorial: Input and Output
text: Using with open(...) as file is recommended for files. The context manager closes the file when the with block finishes, even when an exception occurs.
